## User requirements
The user asked for: **按照以下方向，生成1-2个优质idea，保质不求量：Token-Level Representation Surgery for VLA Robustness
Target: CoRL 2026 (Austin, Nov 9–12, 2026). Abstract deadline 2026-05-26 (12 days from today 2026-05-14); paper deadline 2026-05-29 (15 days).
Direction: Token pruning and augmentation in VLA visual representations — methods that surgically manipulate visual tokens in latent space to improve VLA generalization under realistic perturbations. The core theoretical insight is that VLA visual encoders produce highly redundant token sequences where task-irrelevant tokens (background clutter, static scene regions, occluded areas) dominate attention budgets and create brittle feature correlations. By pruning uninformative tokens and augmenting critical ones in representation space (not pixel space), we compress the effective visual input to a task-relevant manifold that is inherently more robust to distribution shift. Theoretical grounding includes: (1) Information Bottleneck — pruning enforces a tighter bottleneck that retains only task-sufficient statistics, provably improving generalization bounds; (2) Attention Entropy Reduction — concentrating attention mass on fewer, more informative tokens reduces sensitivity to perturbations in pruned regions; (3) Manifold Regularization — augmenting retained tokens along the tangent space of the learned representation manifold provides robustness without leaving the data support. In-scope: adaptive token pruning based on action-relevance scoring, latent-space token augmentation via interpolation/extrapolation on task-critical tokens, attention-guided token selection with theoretical guarantees on information retention, combined prune-and-augment pipelines that maintain action prediction quality while improving robustness to visual distractors, lighting changes, viewpoint shifts, and occlusion.
Recent landscape (do not duplicate): Helix-style self-correction, CacheVLA,LightVLA,TraceVLA, RoboPro, retry/reflection wrappers around VLAs, FastVLA token merging (efficiency-only, no robustness analysis), TokenLearner fixed-count compression. Robustness as benchmark-only is saturated — must propose a method with theoretical motivation.
Contribution type: METHOD ONLY. New training algorithm combining action-conditioned token pruning with latent manifold augmentation: (1) a differentiable token relevance scorer trained with auxiliary action-prediction loss to identify which visual tokens carry task-critical information, (2) a prune-then-augment pipeline that removes low-relevance tokens and performs controlled perturbation of high-relevance tokens in latent space, (3) theoretical analysis showing the pruning step tightens the information bottleneck bound while augmentation smooths the action-prediction landscape, yielding provable robustness margins.
EVAL PROTOCOL — IMPORTANT:
TRAIN on standard LIBERO suites (Object/Spatial/Goal/Long/90).
EVALUATE on existing LIBERO-PLUS / LIBERO-PRO style perturbation benchmarks (and similar community-released robustness benchmark series). DO NOT spend time constructing your own robustness benchmark — use existing perturbation suites and route the budget into the method.
Report robustness gap (Δ between nominal LIBERO success and perturbed-suite success) AND nominal preservation (must not regress on base LIBERO).
Additionally report token reduction ratio vs. robustness improvement curve, and ablate pruning-only vs. augmentation-only vs. combined.
Experiments can be extended to other benchmark series (e.g., CALVIN with perturbation variants) to verify cross-benchmark robustness.
SIM-ONLY MITIGATION: Robustness eval in sim is well-accepted at CoRL — established LIBERO-PLUS / LIBERO-PRO style suites are a recognized sim-only pattern.
HARD CONSTRAINTS:
Compute: ≤200 H100-hours total. Fine-tune from open VLA checkpoints (OpenVLA, SmolVLA, OpenPi, π0) — no pretraining. Token pruning/augmentation adds negligible overhead. Show the math.
Time: ≤20 days. Build on OpenVLA, OpenPi and other proper codebases, LeRobot, HF Transformers.
Eval datasets: LIBERO base (training/nominal eval) + LIBERO-PLUS / LIBERO-PRO and similar existing perturbation suites (perturbed eval). No custom benchmark construction.
Look for: action-conditioned token relevance scoring that adapts per-timestep, latent-space augmentation that exploits the geometry of VLA's representation manifold, information-theoretic pruning criteria with provable bounds, attention entropy as a proxy for robustness, connections between token sparsity and flat minima in action space. Avoid: vanilla pixel-space data augmentation without latent-space method, static/fixed pruning ratios without adaptivity, pure efficiency-motivated token reduction rebranded as robustness, just-add-noise training.

## 论文搜索策略

你的搜索质量直接决定了 idea 的质量。不要敷衍搜索——每一次搜索都要有明确的目的。

### 搜索源（推荐每个维度使用 2 个不同来源）

1. **arXiv 预印本**（最新工作）:
   - `site:arxiv.org {topic} {year}` — 按主题搜索最新论文
   - `site:arxiv.org {method_name}` — 按具体方法名搜索
   - `arxiv {topic} {month} {year}` — 精确到月份，找最近 3 个月的工作

2. **Google Scholar**（引用关系 + 综合覆盖）:
   - `{topic} {year} site:scholar.google.com` — 或直接搜索让 Google 自动包含 Scholar 结果
   - `"{exact paper title}"` — 验证论文是否真实存在
   - `"{author name}" {topic} {year}` — 按活跃作者追踪（找到领域大牛后追踪其最新工作）

3. **Papers With Code**（SOTA 排行 + 代码可用性）:
   - `site:paperswithcode.com {task_name}` — 查看任务的 SOTA 排行榜
   - `site:paperswithcode.com {method_name}` — 查看方法是否已被实现
   - `paperswithcode {dataset} benchmark` — 查看特定 dataset 上的竞争格局

4. **OpenReview**（会议审稿 + 同行评价）:
   - `site:openreview.net {topic} {year}` — 搜索会议提交的论文
   - 用 WebFetch 阅读 OpenReview 上的 reviewer comments — 了解领域专家的真实评价

5. **Semantic Scholar**（语义搜索 + 引用图谱）:
   - `semantic scholar {topic} survey {year}` — 找综述论文
   - `semanticscholar.org {paper_title}` — 查看 cited by（谁引用了这篇）和 references（它引用了谁）

6. **GitHub**（实现验证）:
   - `site:github.com {method_name} {task}` — 验证开源实现是否存在
   - `site:huggingface.co {model_name}` — 验证模型/数据集是否可获取

### 搜索维度（多角度交叉，不要只按 topic 搜）

对每个 idea/方向，尽量覆盖以下维度：

1. **正向搜索**：直接搜索主题相关论文
   - `{topic} {subtopic} {year}`
   - `{method_name} for {task_name}`

2. **竞争论文搜索**（最关键！）：
   - `{core_problem} {year}` — 有没有人在解决同样的问题？
   - `{approach_keyword} {task} {year}` — 有没有人用类似方法？
   - `{gap_description} solution` — 你发现的 gap 是否已被解决？
   - **搜索知名团队的最新工作**：如果你知道哪些团队在做这个方向，搜索他们最近 6 个月的论文

3. **相邻领域搜索**：
   - `{method_from_other_field} applied to {your_task}`
   - `{your_problem} in {adjacent_domain}` — 其他领域是否已解决类似问题

4. **反面搜索**（找到反对你 idea 的证据）：
   - `{your_approach} limitations` / `{your_approach} failure`
   - `why {assumed_gap} is not a problem`
   - `{baseline_method} sufficient for {task}` — baseline 是否其实已经够好

5. **引用链追踪**（发现遗漏工作的最有效方法）：
   - 找到一篇核心相关论文后，用 WebFetch 阅读它的 references 部分
   - 在 Semantic Scholar 上查看它的 "cited by" — 最近引用它的论文很可能是 concurrent work
   - 对 3 个以上核心相关论文重复此步骤

### 搜索数量建议（理想目标，上下文充裕时尽量达到）

| 角色 | 建议搜索次数 | 说明 |
|------|-------------|------|
| Round 1 Generator | 10-15 次 | 每个方向争取 3 次独立搜索 |
| Round 2 Generator | 5-8 次 | 验证 approach 可行性 + baseline |
| Review Agent | 8-12 次 | 独立验证 + 竞争论文 + 反面证据 |
| Revision Agent | 5-10 次 | 针对每个 issue 独立调研 |

### 上下文管理

你的输出 token 有限，必须在上下文耗尽之前完成 JSON 输出。

- 上述搜索次数是理想目标。在上下文充裕时应尽量多搜、深搜，搜得越充分越好。
- 但必须动态评估剩余上下文：如果已经消耗了大量上下文，应优先完成输出，不要为了凑次数而冒着无法输出的风险。
- WebFetch 深度阅读很有价值，但每次 fetch 消耗大量 token——优先 fetch 最关键的 2-3 篇，而不是每篇都 fetch。
- 质量 > 数量：5 次精准搜索 + 深度思考 > 15 次浅层搜索。

   - 不同粒度（e.g., 'text classification' → 'sentiment analysis' → 'NLP'）
   - 方法名 + 任务名的不同组合

   - `{conference_name} 2026 accepted papers {topic}`

4. **arXiv 近 3 个月密集搜索**：对精确相关的关键词，搜索过去 3 个月的 arXiv 论文
   这是发现 concurrent work 最有效的窗口

如果你发现了 Generator 遗漏的重要相关工作，必须在 issues 中列出论文标题和链接，
并在 feedback 中说明这些工作如何影响 idea 的 novelty。

## Review checklist
1. **SOTA freshness**: Are the models/baselines cited actually current SOTA?
   If outdated, specify what the current SOTA is and cite your source.
2. **Reference verification**: Do the cited papers actually exist? (WebSearch to check)
3. **Gap validity**: Does the claimed research gap still exist, or has recent work addressed it?
4. **Venue validity**: Are target_venues' submission deadlines after 2026-05-14?
5. **Feasibility**: Is the resource estimate realistic? Are there hidden dependencies?
6. **Novelty**: Is this sufficiently different from existing work?
   When scoring novelty < 4:
   - You MUST identify the closest existing work(s) via WebSearch
   - In your feedback, write: "This idea is too similar to [Paper Title (Venue Year)]. Specifically, [what overlaps]. To differentiate, the generator should [suggestion]."
   - This gives the generator targeted guidance to boost novelty, not just "be more novel".
7. **Cost realism across modes**: Are the three mode estimates (manual/human-in-loop/auto) internally consistent?
   - Auto Research uses more GPU hours (2-5x manual) but GPU idle rate should be near zero
   - Auto Research timeline should reflect resource availability as bottleneck — days with sufficient GPUs, not weeks
   - Human-in-Loop should fall between manual and auto on most dimensions
   - Manual and HIL must NOT include salary/wages — only GPU and API costs
   - Auto Research must NOT include agent operational overhead
   - If any mode estimate is clearly unrealistic, flag it

Here is a thorough verification of the paper and its claims:

## 1. Paper Existence and Claims

**The paper exists.** Full title: "VLA Models Are More Generalizable Than You Think: Revisiting Physical and Spatial Modeling" (arXiv:2512.02902). Authors: Weiqi Li, Quande Zhang, Ruifeng Zhai, Liang Lin, Guangrun Wang (Sun Yat-sen University, funded partly by Huawei Strategic Research Institute). Originally submitted December 2, 2025; revised March 31, 2026.

**Core thesis:** The brittleness of VLA models under novel viewpoints stems from misalignment in *Spatial Modeling* (the visual encoder's spatial representations), NOT from *Physical Modeling* (the VLM reasoning and action generation). They argue that enhancing robustness "does not require larger models or more data; instead, efficient, targeted adaptation can unlock the inherent generalization potential of existing VLA architectures."

## 2. FTM 87.1% Viewpoint Robustness Claim -- VERIFIED (with caveats)

**The 87.1% number is real, but context matters:**

- The baseline pi0.5 zero-shot accuracy on novel camera viewpoints in LIBERO is **48.5%**.
- FTM improves this to **87.1%** using only **4,096 parameters (4K)** -- this is confirmed.
- However, this is specifically the *novel camera viewpoint* column of the LIBERO-V benchmark, not the overall LIBERO-V average.
- The overall LIBERO-V average for FTM is **90.5%** (because the model already performs well on lighting, texture, and noise perturbations without adaptation -- 96.0%, 96.0%, and 93.6% respectively).
- For comparison, full LoRA fine-tuning of pi0.5 achieves **90.3%** on viewpoints with **467M parameters**, making FTM roughly 117,000x more parameter-efficient for a similar viewpoint result.

## 3. "Input-Independent" Claim -- VERIFIED

**FTM is explicitly input-independent.** The paper states: "unlike conditional modulation methods that generate input-dependent parameters, our gamma and beta are globally applied yet learnable, jointly optimized during adaptation while keeping the backbone frozen."

The formula is: **F_hat = (1 + gamma) . F + beta**, where gamma and beta are in R^{D_ViT}. These are two fixed learnable vectors that apply the exact same affine transformation to every visual token of every input image. There is no conditioning on the input whatsoever. The authors frame this as "a controlled probe to examine whether viewpoint brittleness primarily originates from embedding misalignment rather than insufficient model capacity."

This is indeed surprising -- the same global shift/scale applied to all inputs nearly recovers full viewpoint robustness.

## 4. Base Model -- pi0.5, VERIFIED

The paper uses **pi0.5** (from Physical Intelligence) as the primary base model, with comparisons to **pi0** and **OpenVLA**. The pi0.5 architecture is decomposed into three modules: visual encoder f_v, language encoder f_l, and multimodal transformer decoder. The paper references pi0.5 as "a vision-language-action model with open-world generalization" (arXiv:2504.16054). The exact model size is not specified in the paper.

## 5. Limitations -- THE PAPER HAS NO DEDICATED LIMITATIONS SECTION

This is notable. The paper does **not** contain an explicit "Limitations," "Broader Impact," or "Future Work" section. Section 6 is the conclusion followed by acknowledgments and references. However, implicit limitations can be inferred:

- **FTM has a performance ceiling:** 87.1% viewpoint accuracy vs. 90.8% for FLA and 90.3% for LoRA. The global affine transform cannot capture all viewpoint-induced changes.
- **One-shot requirement:** Adaptation still requires one human demonstration per task from the new viewpoint (trained for 2000 steps, batch size 32, or 750 steps for real-world).
- **Theoretical assumptions:** Their Theorem 1 relies on assumptions of locally Lipschitz policy behavior, task semantic invariance, and locally affine/low-rank structure between source and target distributions -- described as "mild and empirically verifiable" but still assumptions.
- **Task-specific variation:** FLA performance varies: Spatial 95.5%, Object 97.5%, Goal 91.7%, but Long-horizon tasks only 77.5%.
- **No zero-shot generalization:** FTM/FLA require adaptation data; they do not solve the zero-shot viewpoint generalization problem.

| Method | Params | Camera | Light | Texture | Noise | Avg |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Method | Parameters | LIBERO-V Success |
|---|---|---|
| Prompt Learning | 0.131M | 75.1% |
| FTM | 0.004M | 90.5% |
| FLA | 4.7M | 94.8% |
| pi0.5 LoRA | 467M | 94.6% |

## Verification Report

### Paper 1: BC-IB (arXiv 2502.02853)

**Title:** "Rethinking Latent Redundancy in Behavior Cloning: An Information Bottleneck Approach for Robot Manipulation"
**Authors:** Shuanghao Bai, Wanqi Zhou, Pengxiang Ding, Wei Zhao, Donglin Wang, Badong Chen

**Does this paper exist? Is it really ICML 2025?**
- YES. The paper exists at arXiv 2502.02853 and is confirmed accepted at ICML 2025. It also appears in the ICML 2025 proceedings at `proceedings.mlr.press/v267/bai25e.html` and has an official GitHub repo at `github.com/BaiShuanghao/BC-IB` labeled "[ICML 2025]".

**Does it apply IB at the representation level (not token level)?**
- YES. The IB is applied at the **latent representation level**, not the token level. Specifically, the method concatenates features extracted from all modalities through respective feature extractors into input X, then obtains compressed representation Z via a fusion network, and minimizes the mutual information between X and Z. The information flow is O -> X -> Z -> A, where the bottleneck sits between feature extraction and policy decoding. It compresses **representations after spatial/temporal fusion modules** (MLPs, RNNs, or Transformers), not individual tokens within attention mechanisms.

**Does it achieve +5.6% on LIBERO?**
- APPROXIMATELY. The paper does not state a single "+5.6%" figure. The actual improvements across methods on LIBERO (averaged over all four suites) are:
  - BC-MLP+IB: +8.92%
  - BC-RNN+IB: +5.08%
  - BC-Transformer+IB: +4.22%
  - BC-VILT+IB: **+5.58%**
  - Overall average across all methods: roughly **+5.95%**
  
  The BC-VILT+IB result (+5.58%) is closest to the claimed +5.6%. The overall average is ~5.95%. So "+5.6%" is a reasonable but slightly rounded characterization, likely referring to BC-VILT specifically.

**Does it explicitly mention domain-shift robustness as an open problem?**
- YES. In Section 6 (Limitations and Discussion), the paper explicitly states: *"its robustness to domain shifts, including changes in environment and task configurations, remains insufficiently studied."* This is framed as a limitation and open direction for future research.

---

### Paper 2: DRIBO (arXiv 2102.13268)

**Title:** "DRIBO: Robust Deep Reinforcement Learning via Multi-View Information Bottleneck"
**Authors:** Jiameng Fan, Wenchao Li

**Does this paper exist? Is it really ICML 2022?**
- YES. The paper exists at arXiv 2102.13268 and was presented as a poster at ICML 2022. It appears in the official proceedings at `proceedings.mlr.press/v162/fan22b`. The ICML virtual site confirms it: `icml.cc/virtual/2022/poster/16441`.

**Does it use augmentation-generated paired views with contrastive MIB?**
- YES. The paper explicitly generates multi-view pairs via **stochastic data augmentation** (specifically random crops) applied to the same observation. Algorithm 1 states: "Apply random augmentation transformations on B to obtain multi-view batches B^(1) and B^(2)." The paper then introduces a **contrastive version of the Multi-View Information Bottleneck (MIB) objective** using InfoNCE for mutual information estimation. Positive pairs are representations from the same observation under different augmentations. The loss combines: (1) mutual information maximization between representation sequences from different views, and (2) symmetrized KL divergence minimization to compress task-irrelevant information.

**Does it operate at representation level, not token level?**
- YES. The method uses an **RSSM (Recurrent State Space Model) encoder** that processes pixel observations into latent state representations. The contrastive MIB objective is applied to these encoded latent representations, not to raw pixels or individual tokens. The two augmented views are encoded separately to produce two representation sequences, and the MIB loss operates on those representation vectors. As the paper states: "DRIBO uses a multi-view information bottleneck loss to maximize the task-relevant information shared between representations." The core assumption is: "any information not shared by [the two views] are considered task-irrelevant."

---

| Claim | Verified? |
|-------|-----------|
| BC-IB exists at arXiv 2502.02853 | YES |
| BC-IB is ICML 2025 | YES |
| BC-IB applies IB at representation level, not token level | YES |
| BC-IB achieves +5.6% on LIBERO | APPROXIMATELY -- +5.58% for BC-VILT, ~5.95% average across methods |
| BC-IB mentions domain-shift robustness as open problem | YES -- explicit quote in Limitations section |
| DRIBO exists at arXiv 2102.13268 | YES |
| DRIBO is ICML 2022 | YES |
| DRIBO uses augmentation-generated paired views with contrastive MIB | YES -- random crops, InfoNCE-based contrastive MIB |
| DRIBO operates at representation level, not token level | YES -- RSSM encoder, IB on latent representations |

All major claims check out. The only minor caveat is that the "+5.6% on LIBERO" is not a single headline number from the paper but rather a reasonable approximation of BC-VILT+IB's average improvement (+5.58%) or a slight underestimate of the cross-method average (+5.95%).
